question:
Which of the following diagrams depicts the positions of the ureters (shown as blue lines) and the urinary bladder in the human excretory system?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a2c9e0587a7ada0f42877a89db00131f650100a533fab928901e314c00c8fd1f.png]
solution:
The **correct** answer is __**Diagram 1**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ureteropelvic** junction (UPJ), which is located **posterior** to the renal vein and artery in the hilum, is where the ureters are first** formed**.
 
• The **ureters** then move inferiorly within the **abdominal cavity**.
 
• They enter the bladder on the **posterior bladder** aspect in the trigone after passing across the **psoas muscle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functions** of **Bladders**:

 
 
• The **lower abdomen** contains this hollow, **triangle-shaped **organ.
 
• **Ligaments** that are connected to various **organs** and the pelvic bones hold it in place.
 
• The bladder's walls **flatten** and constrict to empty pee through the **urethra** after relaxing and expanding to store urine.
 
 
 
• Functions of** ****ureters**:
 
 
• Urine is emptied into the bladder every **10 to 15 seconds** by the continuously active **ureters**.
 
• The kidneys play a number of roles in the body, including **balancing **fluid levels, releasing hormones to control blood pressure, and regulating the generation of** red blood cells**.
 
• **Urine travels **from the renal pelvis into the **bladder** through the urinary tract, which is connected to the kidneys by two thin (3 to 4 mm) tubular structures **called ureters**.
 
• The **peristaltic activity**, which is used by the ureter to** transport urine** from the kidneys to the bladder, is brought on by the** muscular layers**.
